originalSourceText:
Q.8  A robot uses the traditional pipeline:
      Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) →Large Language Model (LLM) → Text-to-
      Speech (TTS)
         If the ASR incorrectly transcribes “turn right” as “turn light,” which downstream
      consequence is most consistent?

      (A) The LLM is guaranteed to recover the original audio signal.

      (B) The transcription error can propagate into the LLM and affect the generated
       response/action.

      (C) TTS automatically corrects the semantic error.

      (D) The error disappears because ASR and LLM are independent.

       Explanation: Cumulative error as a major limitation: transcription errors from ASR
      can cascade into the LLM.
      Refer slide 17 of Lecture 49: Conversational AI & Human-Robot Interaction
